Electrodiagnostic Classification of Sensory Neuropathies: Severity Clusters and Clinical Correlates.
papers.abstract: Grading sensory neuropathy severity on nerve conduction studies (NCS) is operator dependent, which limits comparisons across patients, laboratories, and studies. We aimed to develop an objective severity classification to standardize NCS reporting and support clinical decision-making. We retrospectively analyzed NCS performed at IRCCS San Raffaele Hospital (2018-2024), extracted with a validated parser. Adult studies with sensory involvement were selected using sural sensory nerve action potential (SNAP) amplitude thresholds after excluding motor abnormalities. Hierarchical clustering combined normalized sural and "best" upper-limb (UL) SNAP amplitudes with binary indicators for absent responses. Classes were ordered by an NCS severity index and validated against clinical scales. Among 15,744 consecutive examinations, 308 met inclusion criteria. Three well-separated NCS severity classes emerged: mild (reduced but present sural and present UL SNAPs), moderate (absent sural, present UL SNAPs), and severe (absent sural and UL SNAPs). Clinical severity increased monotonically across classes. Patients in the severe class had younger age at symptom onset than those in mild-moderate classes and were more disabled (modified Rankin scale ≥ 2: 50.0% in severe vs 30.4% in moderate vs 16.2% in mild). The severe class was enriched in immune/paraneoplastic (12.5%) and genetic (40.6%) causes. By stratifying patients based on SNAP amplitudes, we identified a differential etiologic enrichment rather than a continuum of disease progression. Severe electrophysiology with motor sparing should prompt RFC1 testing and immune/paraneoplastic work-up, whereas mild to moderate abnormalities should lead to assessment for diabetes and toxic or nutritional exposures.

papers.title: Wearable Evidence Linking Dyskinesia Burden to Sleep Quality in Parkinson's Disease.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances affect 60-80% of people with Parkinson's disease (PD) and worsen quality of life. Dyskinesia is a common complication of dopaminergic therapy, yet its link to sleep quality is poorly understood. To examine whether clinician-rated and objectively measured dyskinesia are associated with sleep quality in PD. We studied 47 people with PD (median age 68 years; 44.7% women; median disease duration 5 years). Sleep was measured with Pittsburgh Sleep Quality Index (PSQI). Dyskinesia was rated clinically (MDS-UPDRS items 4.1, 4.2) and objectively over 7 days using Parkinson's KinetiGraph (median dyskinesia score; DKS). Regression models adjusted for age, sex, motor severity, levodopa dose, and disease duration. All dyskinesia measures predicted poorer sleep unadjusted. After adjusting for levodopa dose, only DKS remained significant (B = 0.18, P = 0.047). Adding disease duration attenuated this (P = 0.051). Wearable-derived dyskinesia, but not clinician-rated dyskinesia, independently predicted poorer sleep, supporting wearable monitoring in PD.

papers.title: Objective sleep characteristics and longitudinal change in financial and health literacy in older adults.
papers.abstract: Sleep disturbances are common in older adults and linked to cognitive decline, but their association with functional abilities such as financial and health literacy is less understood. Participants without dementia from the Rush Memory and Aging Project (N = 765) completed annual literacy assessments. Baseline sleep measures included self-reported nighttime sleep duration, actigraphy-derived nighttime sleep duration, and actigraphy-derived daytime napping. Linear mixed-effects models examined associations with literacy change. Literacy declined by ≈ 1 percentage point per year. Longer nighttime sleep was associated with higher baseline literacy and with slower decline in single-predictor models, but the decline association was attenuated and no longer statistically significant after adjustment for daytime napping. Greater daytime napping was associated with slower decline but not baseline literacy. Self-reported sleep was not associated with literacy trajectories, although short sleep (< 6 hours) was linked to lower baseline literacy. Objective sleep characteristics were associated with financial and health literacy trajectories in older adults, suggesting that sleep behavior may be related to changes in financial and health decision-making abilities.

papers.title: Psychiatry of ophthalmology: Proposing the ophthalmo-psychiatric disorders framework.
papers.abstract: We propose the ophthalmo-psychiatric disorders (OPD) framework as an organizing clinical and research model at the interface of vision science and mental health, and to synthesize, with wording calibrated to evidence strength, bidirectional relationships between ophthalmic disease, visual function, and psychiatric states. Visual impairment and common mental disorders co-distribute globally, with adults with vision loss showing roughly two-to three-fold higher prevalence of depressive and anxiety symptoms than visually normal peers. Elevated psychiatric comorbidity across glaucoma, dry eye disease, and age-related macular degeneration is supported by systematic reviews and meta-analyses, as is the benefit of psychological and stepped-care intervention. Mechanistic claims are weaker: hypothalamic-pituitary-adrenal and autonomic dysregulation, inflammation, circadian disruption, central sensitization, and retinal neurodegeneration remain candidate pathways resting largely on cross-sectional data, and retinal findings in severe mental illness are group-level associations confounded by lifestyle, metabolic, medication, and imaging factors. The eye and the mind are anatomically and physiologically connected. The concept of OPD provides a pragmatic biopsychosocial framework that moves beyond an "organic versus non-organic (functional)" dichotomy and highlights the clinical intersection of the 2 fields. Progress will depend on interdisciplinary training, longitudinal research with harmonized definitions, and culturally sensitive implementation of eye-mind care.

papers.title: Adjunctive perampanel in children with focal-onset seizures and developmental delay or intellectual disability: efficacy, tolerability, and sleep benefits.
papers.abstract: Perampanel (PER), a noncompetitive alpha-amino-3-hydroxy-5-methyl-4-isoxazolepropionic acid receptor antagonist, is used to treat focal-onset seizures in patients aged ≥4 years. However, evidence in children with focal-onset seizures and developmental delay (DD) and/or intellectual disability (ID) remains limited, particularly regarding sleep-related outcomes. This study evaluated the efficacy and tolerability of adjunctive PER in this population. This retrospective single-cohort study assessed the effectiveness of adjunctive PER for overall and sleep-related seizures and sleep disturbance, as well as tolerability based on adverse events and treatment retention, in patients aged <18 years with focal-onset seizures and DD/ID treated from January 2020 through December 2025. Among 83 screened patients, 57 who received PER for >3 months were included. Genetic etiology was most common (23/57, 40.4%), and 91.2% had drug-resistant epilepsy. Sleep-related seizures occurred in 73.7%, and sleep disturbance was present in 50.9%. Hypersomnolence (29.8%) and aggression (24.6%) were the most common adverse events, and 51 patients (89.5%) remained on PER for ≥12 months. Overall responder rates (≥50% seizure reduction) at 3, 6, and 12 months were 89.5% (51/57), 81.1% (43/53), and 74.5% (38/51), with seizure-free rates of 45.6%, 49.1%, and 43.1%, respectively. Corresponding responder rates for sleep-related seizures were 92.9%, 89.7%, and 76.9% (39/42, 35/39, and 30/39), with seizure-free rates of 40.5%, 46.2%, and 30.8%. Among 29 patients with preexisting sleep disturbance, 93.1% improved. Adjunctive PER demonstrated favorable effectiveness and tolerability in children with focal-onset seizures and DD/ID despite substantial drug resistance and was also associated with improvement in sleep disturbance.

papers.title: Novel sleep scoring method for neurodegenerative diseases: feasibility and reliability in advanced Parkinson disease.
papers.abstract: In neurodegenerative diseases, damage to sleep-wake regulating brain regions alters sleep architecture (e.g., loss of spindles and K-complexes, EEG slowing during wakefulness and REM sleep), challenging the current American Academy of Sleep Medicine (AASM) rules for scoring sleep. In Parkinson disease (PD) patients, we assessed the feasibility and interrater reliability of a previously described novel sleep scoring methodology. Video-polysomnography of 15 PD patients and five age-matched controls were scored blinded by five trained raters (two neurologists and three technicians) with different levels of expertise. Recordings were first scored empirically following the AASM methodology and, when necessary, scored again using the following additional abnormal stages: abnormal Wake, Subwake, Undifferentiated NREM (UNREM) sleep, Poorly Structured N2 sleep, and abnormal REM sleep. Sleep microstructure alterations (e.g., encapsulated REM sleep behavior disorder) were also evaluated. The novel scoring method showed substantial interrater agreement (kappa = 0.75), comparable to the AASM method (kappa = 0.73). UNREM sleep was identified in 12 patients, Subwake in nine, and abnormal Wake, encapsulated REM sleep behavior disorder and abnormal REM sleep in seven. No abnormal stages were observed in three early PD patients or in any control. The presence of the abnormal sleep stages was associated with ageing and advanced PD with cognitive impairment and motor fluctuations. The novel sleep scoring methodology, which includes abnormal wakefulness as well as NREM and REM sleep stages, is feasible, reliable, and applicable in clinical practice for advanced PD patients undergoing video-polysomnography.

papers.title: Objective motion-based performance assessment in STA-MCA microanastomosis: a postprocedural debriefing platform.
papers.abstract: The aim of this study was to develop and demonstrate a postprocedural motion analysis platform capable of objectively quantifying intraoperative surgeon micromovements to facilitate evidence-based self-debriefing in suturing superficial temporal artery-middle cerebral artery microanastomosis. The authors analyzed microscope-recorded microanastomoses performed by a cerebrovascular neurosurgeon. Seven suture-placement clips were extracted from operative videos. A computer vision tracking pipeline was implemented in Python using OpenCV to track the needle holder position across the video clips. Four motion metrics were computed for each video clip: absolute error, velocity, acceleration, and jerk. A unified reference distribution was constructed from all clips, and 95th percentile thresholds were defined for each metric. The metrics were displayed as dynamic synchronized plots alongside the corresponding video. Spectral decomposition of the position signal was performed to generate time-frequency representations, and average power in the 6- to 8-Hz band was computed as a quantitative tremor measure. To demonstrate reliable longitudinal performance tracking, the authors applied their platform to 8 recorded procedures between 2023 and 2026 and plotted the mean jerk per suture over time. Reliable tracking was achieved across 92.09% of analyzed footage. Two-dimensional trajectories were reconstructed for a total of 13,183 analyzed frames encompassing 219.82 seconds of suture-placement video (7 clips). Jerk analysis revealed multiple segments exceeding the 95th percentile threshold, flagging moments for surgical review. Time-frequency analysis revealed transient broadband power bursts and 2 persistent spectral bands (6-8 Hz and < 4 Hz). Tremor intensity analysis in the 6- to 8-Hz range revealed temporal tremor fluctuations, a finding undetectable by other metrics. Longitudinal performance tracking was feasible and demonstrated a stable jerk profile, consistent with expert-level performance. A motion-based postprocedural debriefing platform for the performance of microanastomosis is technically feasible and capable of generating objective, quantitative performance metrics from standard operative video. Unlike prior work focused on expert-novice differentiation, this platform was designed to support individualized self-assessment and reflective practice for surgeons at any experience level. Future work should validate the platform prospectively and correlate motion-based metrics with clinical outcomes.

papers.title: Machine Learning Classification of Bipolar Disorder Across Mood States Using Natural Language Processing and Speech Analysis: Observational Study.
papers.abstract: Bipolar disorder (BP) affects 1% to 3% of adults worldwide, with diagnostic delays averaging 6 years and high initial misdiagnosis rates. The absence of objective diagnostic measures contributes to clinical uncertainty and suboptimal outcomes. This study aimed to (1) develop a machine learning model for BP diagnosis and mood state classification using linguistic and acoustic features, (2) identify features associated with different mood states by comparing each with healthy controls (HC), and (3) explore whether features distinguish between mood states within BP. We analyzed data prospectively collected over 7 years from 61 patients with BP and 99 HC across Japan. Speech samples were collected via semistructured interviews over 1 to 5 visits and analyzed cross-sectionally, using aggregated or single-visit observations per participant rather than within-person longitudinal modeling. We extracted 6373 acoustic features (openSMILE 3.0, ComParE 2016) and 211 linguistic features. Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO)-regularized logistic regression with nested cross-validation and age- and sex-matched undersampling was used. Mood states were classified as depressive state (DS; Hamilton Depression Rating Scale-17 [HAMD-17] ≥8, Young Mania Rating Scale [YMRS] ≤7), state with manic/mixed symptoms (MS/MX; YMRS ≥8), or euthymic state (ES; HAMD-17 ≤7, YMRS ≤7). Seven classification tasks included BP vs HC, each mood state vs HC, and interstate comparisons. Feature importance was validated via permutation testing (P<.05). Medication sensitivity analyses were performed. The model achieved high discrimination for BP vs HC (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [AUC]=0.916, 95% CI 0.854-0.958; sensitivity 0.933; specificity 0.859) and strong performance for mood states vs HC (AUC=0.805-0.874). Acoustic features comprised 96% to 98% of the features achieving statistical significance (P<.05), including mel-frequency cepstral coefficients, spectral characteristics, and voice quality measures, showing strong correlations with diagnostic probabilities (|ρ|=0.35-0.85) and symptom severity (HAMD-17: ρ=-0.51; YMRS: ρ=-0.37); 2 to 4 linguistic features per comparison also reached significance. With sample independence ensured for interstate comparisons, DS vs ES significantly exceeded chance (AUC=0.760, permutation P=.03), whereas MS/MX vs ES (AUC=0.601, P=.20) and DS vs MS/MX (AUC=0.569, P=.30) did not, suggesting that markers primarily reflect persistent disease characteristics with partial state-associated components in depressive states. The combined acoustic-linguistic model, driven primarily by acoustic features, shows potential as an objective aid for BP diagnosis (AUC>0.9), largely free of medication confounding; some features remained detectable during euthymia, although ES discrimination could not be fully separated from concurrent antipsychotic treatment. Although DS showed partial distinguishability from ES, overall limitations remain for monitoring mood state changes. Findings require validation in diverse populations and against other psychiatric conditions.

papers.title: Reported Life-Threatening Polymorphic Ventricular Arrhythmia With Torsade-Like Morphology in a Patient With Gordon Syndrome and Hyperkalaemia.
papers.abstract: Gordon's syndrome (pseudohypoaldosteronism type II) is a rare, inherited tubulopathy characterised by salt-sensitive hypertension, hyperkalaemia, and metabolic acidosis despite preserved renal function. Pathogenic variants affecting the with-no-lysine (K) signalling pathway include WNK1, WNK4, KLHL3, and CUL3. We report the case of a 37-year-old woman with genetically confirmed CUL3-related Gordon's syndrome who developed hyperkalaemia after a three-week interruption of bendroflumethiazide. During pre-hospital assessment, ambulance clinicians documented a self-terminating rhythm that they identified as torsade de pointes. The original recording cannot be retrieved; consequently, the rhythm classification, preceding QT interval, and possible alternative rhythm or artefact could not be independently assessed. Point-of-care venous blood gas potassium was 4.8 mmol/L, whereas formal laboratory potassium was 6.1 mmol/L. The sampling and processing information available did not establish the cause of this discrepancy. Subsequent echocardiography, computed tomography coronary angiography, cardiac magnetic resonance imaging, ambulatory monitoring, exercise testing, and additional electrical assessment did not identify a definitive alternative substrate, although an intermittent electrical disorder could not be excluded. Following treatment of hyperkalaemia and multidisciplinary cardiology and electrophysiology review, an extravascular implantable cardioverter-defibrillator was implanted. Bendroflumethiazide was resumed, with subsequent improvement in potassium control. This case highlights the importance of uninterrupted thiazide therapy in Gordon's syndrome, assessment of discordant potassium measurements, and careful interpretation of a reported serious rhythm event when its original tracing is unavailable. The temporal association with hyperkalaemia does not establish that it caused torsade de pointes.

papers.title: Clinical Symptom Burden and Its Association With Echocardiographic Parameters and Comorbidities in Heart Failure With Preserved Ejection Fraction: A Retrospective Study.
papers.abstract: Heart failure with preserved ejection fraction (HFpEF) is a heterogeneous clinical syndrome in which substantial symptoms may occur despite preserved left ventricular ejection fraction (LVEF). Echocardiographic abnormalities involving ventricular filling, left atrial remodeling, diastolic function, and pulmonary pressures may contribute to symptom burden. This study evaluated the association between clinical symptom severity, echocardiographic parameters, and comorbidities in patients with HFpEF. This retrospective observational cross-sectional study was conducted at the Government Peripheral Hospital, Periyar Nagar, Chennai, Tamil Nadu, from March 2025 to March 2026. A total of 216 patients aged ≥18 years with HFpEF and LVEF ≥50% were included. Clinical symptom burden was assessed using New York Heart Association (NYHA) functional class and categorized as I-II or III-IV. Demographic characteristics, comorbidities, and echocardiographic parameters, including LVEF, left ventricular mass, left atrial volume index (LAVI), E/e' ratio, diastolic dysfunction grade, and estimated pulmonary artery systolic pressure (PASP), were evaluated. Multivariable logistic regression identified factors independently associated with NYHA III-IV symptoms. The mean age was 67.8 ± 10.4 years, and 53.7% were female. Hypertension was the most prevalent comorbidity (80.6%), while 76.9% had ≥2 major comorbidities. Fifty-five patients (25.5%) had NYHA III-IV symptoms. Compared with NYHA I-II, the severe symptom group had higher E/e' (17.4 ± 5.0 vs. 12.6 ± 4.0), LAVI (44.5 ± 12.1 vs. 34.2 ± 9.1 mL/m²), LV mass, and PASP (43.9 ± 12.4 vs. 36.8 ± 8.7 mmHg), with significantly more advanced diastolic dysfunction. On multivariable analysis, E/e' (adjusted OR 1.18), LAVI (adjusted OR 1.05), and PASP (adjusted OR 1.04) were independently associated with severe symptoms. Symptom severity in HFpEF was associated more strongly with abnormal filling pressures, left atrial remodeling, and pulmonary hemodynamics than with preserved systolic function alone. E/e', LAVI, and PASP may provide useful complementary markers of symptomatic burden and support a multidimensional echocardiographic assessment of HFpEF.

papers.title: Effect of Preoperative Intranasal Dexmedetomidine on Postoperative Myocardial Injury in Patients Undergoing Coronary Artery Bypass Grafting.
papers.abstract: To evaluate the effects of preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine on postoperative myocardial injury biomarkers in patients undergoing on-pump coronary artery bypass grafting (CABG). In this randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled trial, 70 patients undergoing on-pump CABG were assigned to receive intranasal dexmedetomidine (1 μg/kg) or saline 30 min before bedtime on the night before surgery and again 30 min before anesthesia induction. The primary outcome was serum high-sensitivity cardiac troponin T (hs-cTnT) at 24 h after surgery. Secondary outcomes included perioperative cardiac biomarkers, preoperative sleep quality, postoperative delirium, and adverse events. For the prespecified primary outcome, hs-cTnT concentrations at 24 h after surgery were significantly lower in the dexmedetomidine group than in the control group (estimated marginal means, 170.29 vs 357.29 ng/L; P < 0.001). Postoperative creatine kinase-MB (CK-MB) concentrations were also lower in the dexmedetomidine group (all P < 0.05). N-terminal pro-B-type natriuretic peptide showed a significant group-by-time interaction (P = 0.030), although between-group differences at individual postoperative time points were not significant. The dexmedetomidine group had higher Leeds Sleep Evaluation Questionnaire scores (62 [60-64] vs 44 [41-50]; P < 0.001) and a lower incidence of postoperative delirium (14.3% vs 37.1%; P = 0.029). Adverse events, mechanical ventilation duration, and intensive care unit (ICU) length of stay did not differ significantly between groups. In this single-center trial, two-dose preoperative intranasal dexmedetomidine was associated with lower postoperative hs-cTnT and CK-MB concentrations, better subjective preoperative sleep quality, and a lower observed incidence of postoperative delirium. These findings are preliminary and require confirmation in larger, adequately powered multicenter randomized trials to determine whether the biomarker reductions translate into clinically meaningful cardiovascular benefits. papers.title: Avoiding Diagnostic Pitfalls in Facial Pain: A Case Report of Paroxysmal Hemicrania Initially Treated as Trigeminal Neuralgia.
papers.abstract: A 21-year-old man presented with a two-year history of recurrent, strictly unilateral left-sided pain in the upper maxillary and orbital regions, radiating to the temporal and occipital areas. Individual attacks lasted 20 to 30 minutes and occurred 10 to 20 times daily, on most days throughout the two-year period. He had been diagnosed elsewhere with trigeminal neuralgia and treated with carbamazepine 200 mg twice daily without benefit. He denied photophobia, phonophobia, and ipsilateral cranial autonomic features, but described prominent restlessness during attacks. No cutaneous or mucosal trigger could be identified, and neurological examination was normal. The attack duration, the reported high attack frequency, the absence of tactile triggers, and the restlessness were inconsistent with classical trigeminal neuralgia and raised suspicion of a trigeminal autonomic cephalalgia, including probable paroxysmal hemicrania. Carbamazepine was withdrawn, and an escalating oral indomethacin trial was initiated, reaching 225 mg daily and maintained at that dose for 14 consecutive days. A headache diary begun on the first day of the trial recorded headache on all 20 days, and the patient reported no improvement at any point. Because the phenotype fulfilled all but the indomethacin-response criterion, the diagnosis was recorded as probable paroxysmal hemicrania, while cluster headache and other trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias remained in the differential diagnosis. Verapamil 240 mg daily was substituted on day 21. Headache days fell to 23 of 31 in the first month and 13 of 31 in the second, with the last 18 days of the second month free of headache. At telephone follow-up, the patient reported sustained resolution, with only mild headaches related to sleep deprivation that he considered distinct from his previous syndrome. He remains on verapamil. Whether verapamil produced the improvement cannot be established from a single uncontrolled case, as the drug was never withdrawn, and spontaneous remission remains possible. This case illustrates the clinical overlap between trigeminal neuralgia and the trigeminal autonomic cephalalgias and highlights the value of structured longitudinal symptom recording, ideally including individual attack count, duration, autonomic features, and triggers.

papers.title: First-year changes in mental health, lifestyle behaviors, and social support among international students at a Japanese university.
papers.abstract: International students experience psychological distress due to cultural adjustment, loneliness, and limited social support. However, longitudinal evidence remains scarce in Japan, and comprehensive models incorporating lifestyle and social factors remain underexamined. This study investigated the changes in mental health symptoms, lifestyle behaviors, and social support during international students' first year after university enrollment. Furthermore, we examined longitudinal changes and their associations with academic year repetition. This study included 216 international students who enrolled between 2016 and 2024. They completed questionnaire surveys upon university enrollment and 1 year later. Measures included the Kessler Psychological Distress Scale (K6), suicidal ideation, interpersonal tension, sleep duration, and number of available social supporters. Changes from baseline to 1-year later were examined. Univariable logistic regression analyses were performed with academic year repetition as the outcome and baseline variables and variables that changed as predictors. Of the participants, 1.9% exhibited severe psychological distress (K6 ≥ 13 points) and 15.9% reported suicidal ideation at enrollment. Psychological distress did not significantly change over the first year. However, significant changes were observed in both weekend sleep duration (χ 2 = 28.452, p < 0.001) and weekday sleep duration (χ 2 = 6.838, p = 0.033), fewer available supporters (Z = 2.757, p = 0.006), and reduced interpersonal tension (Z = 2.549, p = 0.011). Furthermore, an increase in weekend sleep duration was associated with academic year repetition (odds ratio [OR] = 3.131, p = 0.027). Reduced interpersonal tension exhibited a trend toward lower repetition risk (OR = 0.131, p = 0.052). Monitoring changes in sleep duration and interpersonal tension after enrollment may enhance academic and mental health support for international students.

papers.title: Effect of Adding Esketamine to Patient-Controlled Intravenous Analgesia on Rebound Pain After Interscalene Brachial Plexus Block: A Randomized Controlled Trial.
papers.abstract: Rebound pain after peripheral nerve block (PNB) may diminish the analgesic benefits of regional anesthesia. Whether esketamine administered via postoperative patient-controlled intravenous analgesia (PCIA) can prevent rebound pain remains unclear. This study aimed to evaluate the effect of esketamine-containing PCIA on rebound pain after interscalene brachial plexus block in patients undergoing shoulder arthroscopic surgery. 132 patients scheduled for arthroscopic shoulder surgery under general anesthesia combined with interscalene brachial plexus block were randomized 1:1 to receive postoperative PCIA with esketamine (1.25 mg/kg) plus sufentanil (100 μg) and flurbiprofen axetil (100 mg) (ES group, n=66) or sufentanil plus flurbiprofen axetil alone (Control group, n=66). The primary outcome was rebound pain, defined as an increase from well-controlled pain (NRS ≤ 3) to severe pain (NRS ≥ 7), typically after resolution of the nerve block. Secondary outcomes included time to rebound pain, modified pain score, rebound pain duration, analgesic consumption, numerical rating scale (NRS) at 6, 12, 24, and 48 h postoperatively, Quality of Recovery-15 (QoR-15), Richards-Campbell Sleep Questionnaire (RCSQ) sleep quality, and adverse events. The incidence of rebound pain did not differ significantly between groups (25.8% vs 39.4%; OR, 0.53; 95% CI, 0.39 to 1.09; P=0.095). Among patients who developed rebound pain, the ES group had a lower modified rebound pain score and shorter pain duration. For other secondary outcomes, patients receiving esketamine had lower NRS pain scores at 12, 24, and 48 h, fewer PCIA demands, less rescue analgesic use, and higher QoR-15 and RCSQ scores (all P<0.05). The incidence of the assessed adverse events did not differ significantly between groups. Adding esketamine to postoperative PCIA did not demonstrate a reduction in rebound pain incidence after interscalene brachial plexus block. Exploratory subgroup findings suggested lower rebound pain intensity and duration, while improvements in postoperative analgesia, sleep, and recovery had uncertain clinical relevance. Further multicenter studies are needed to confirm these findings and to evaluate different dosing strategies and routes of administration.

papers.title: Esketamine as a Perineural Adjuvant to Ropivacaine for Pericapsular Nerve Group (PENG) Block in Elderly Patients Undergoing Hip Fracture Surgery: A Propensity Score-Matched Retrospective Cohort Study.
papers.abstract: Hip fractures are increasing with global aging. We evaluated esketamine as a perineural ropivacaine adjuvant for PENG block on early recovery quality and analgesia in elderly hip fracture surgery patients. In this retrospective cohort study (July 2024-May 2025), 252 elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery under general anesthesia were included. Patients were allocated to control or esketamine groups based on adjuvant use. Propensity score matching yielded 86 pairs. The primary outcome was QoR-15 scores at multiple postoperative time points; secondary outcomes included sensory block duration, sleep quality, pain scores, and adverse events. At 24 and 48 hours, QoR-15 scores were higher with esketamine (median difference, 9 [95% CI, 7-11] and 4 [95% CI, 2-6]). Sensory block was prolonged (16.51 ± 1.30 vs 10.91 ± 1.26 hours; P <0.001). On day 1, sleep quality and VAS pain scores improved (both P <0.001), but neither difference exceeded the population-specific MCID. Time to first ambulation was shorter, and intraoperative propofol and remifentanil use was lower (both P <0.001). Frailty, age, anxiety, and higher aCCI predicted unfavorable recovery trajectories. Among elderly patients undergoing hip fracture surgery, esketamine added to ropivacaine for PENG block improved 24-hour recovery quality (QoR-15, exceeding MCID; 48-hour scores higher but below MCID), prolonged sensory block, shortened time to first ambulation, and reduced intraoperative anesthetic and opioid use. Sleep and analgesia improved only at 24 hours but did not exceed population-specific MCIDs. No difference in adverse events was detected within sample size constraints. In an exploratory latent trajectory analysis of the control group, frailty, age, anxiety, and aCCI predicted poor recovery.

papers.title: Mood and Behavioral Changes in Adult Cerebral X-linked Adrenoleukodystrophy.
papers.abstract: A 33-year-old man with genetically confirmed X-linked adrenoleukodystrophy developed progressive irritability, emotional lability, anger outbursts, repetitive reassurance-seeking, and insomnia alongside worsening spastic paraparesis and urinary symptoms. Difficulty recalling familiar names and remembering and completing assigned tasks subsequently impaired occupational functioning. Collateral history established a departure from his calm and socially appropriate premorbid personality. Behavioral examination revealed overfamiliarity, disinhibited language, emotional lability, impaired judgment, and perseverative illness-related preoccupation. Cognitive examination demonstrated impaired attention, set-shifting, verbal fluency, inhibitory control, new learning, and recent recall, while neurological examination revealed pyramidal signs and a spastic gait. Brain magnetic resonance imaging showed symmetrical posterior cerebral white-matter hyperintensities, and genetic testing identified an ABCD1 c.323C>A variant. The temporal association with neurological progression, acquired behavioral change, cognitive impairment, and characteristic imaging abnormalities supported secondary mood syndrome with accompanying behavioral and cognitive manifestations rather than a primary depressive episode or adjustment disorder. Irritability, sleep, and anger outbursts improved during approximately one week of inpatient treatment with supportive intervention, low-dose quetiapine, and sodium valproate, although post-discharge follow-up was unavailable. This case emphasizes that new affective, behavioral, or cognitive symptoms in cerebral white-matter disease should prompt collateral history-taking, cognitive and neurological examination, and reassessment for disease progression.

papers.title: Perceptual lengthening of visual time throughout learning of hand-reaching actions.
papers.abstract: Timing is intimately woven into human cognition and behavior, yet the dynamic interplay between timing and action remains poorly understood, particularly during goal-directed action learning. Using combined behavioral, electroencephalographic, and modeling approaches, we investigated how perceptual time changes as participants gained experience in a goal-directed reaching task requiring different degrees of action planning. Participants judged brief visual durations while preparing hand movements toward visual targets. Subjective time expanded during action preparation, which gradually increased across trials mirroring gradual improvements in action readiness. Representational similarity analysis revealed dissociable neural responses linking action and timing: action planning influenced time encoding during timed stimulus presentation, whereas broader motor engagement shaped subsequent time decoding following stimulus presentation. These findings extend previous accounts of action-dependent changes in perceived time, showing that the interaction is dynamic, evolving with changes in action readiness, and is mediated by dissociable neural responses during time encoding and decoding stages.

papers.title: Prevalence of Sleep Disorders in Patients With Knee, Hip, and Hand Osteoarthritis: A Systematic Review With Meta-Analysis.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: To estimate the pooled prevalences of insomnia, obstructive sleep apnea, restless legs syndrome, and narcolepsy in patients with knee, hip, or hand osteoarthritis. DESIGN: Prevalence systematic review with meta-analyses. The review protocol was preregistered at PROSPERO (CRD420251005836). LITERATURE SEARCH: We conducted systematic searches in Embase, MEDLINE, and the Cochrane Library from inception to August 2025, supplemented by citation screening and reference checking. STUDY SELECTION CRITERIA: We identified observational and interventional studies reporting prevalence data on sleep disorders among patients with knee, hip, or hand osteoarthritis. DATA SYNTHESIS: Risk of bias was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using the Grading of Recommendations Assessment, Development, and Evaluation tool. Pooled prevalence estimates were calculated using random-effects proportion meta-analyses, with subgroup analyses based on diagnostic criteria and patient characteristics. RESULTS: Eighteen studies (202 847 participants) were included (three cohort, five case-control, 12 cross-sectional), of which nine studies were of very good to good or high quality. Insomnia was the most prevalent sleep disorder, 42% (95% confidence interval [CI]: 34% to 51%), followed by sleep apnea (37% [95% CI: 6% to 67%]) and restless legs syndrome (35% [95% CI: 10% to 61%]). No studies reported on narcolepsy. Estimates varied by diagnostic criteria and sample characteristics across studies, and the certainty of evidence was very low. CONCLUSION: Sleep disorders, particularly insomnia, were common among patients with knee, hip, or hand osteoarthritis, supporting the need to raise clinical awareness. Future studies may alter prevalence estimates, as only a small number of high-quality studies were identified and large between-study heterogeneity was observed. papers.title: Sleep architecture disruption and coordinated patterns of inflammatory and extracellular matrix biomarkers in obstructive sleep apnea: a cross-sectional study.
papers.abstract: This study aimed to investigate the associations between circulating inflammatory, extracellular matrix (ECM), and oxidative stress biomarkers and polysomnographic parameters across different severity levels of obstructive sleep apnea (OSA), with adjustment for body mass index (BMI). Seventy adults with confirmed OSA were categorized as mild-to-moderate or severe based on apnea-hypopnea index (AHI). Serum levels of TNF-α, IL-6, MMP-2, MMP-9, desmosine, cellular fibronectin (cFN), syndecan-1 (SDC-1), glutathione (GSH), and malondialdehyde (MDA) were measured using ELISA or spectrophotometric methods. Biomarker concentrations were natural-log transformed to satisfy normality assumptions; between-group comparisons were adjusted for BMI using ANCOVA. Associations among biomarkers and clinical variables were assessed using Spearman correlation, BMI-adjusted partial correlation, and network analysis. Severe OSA was associated with higher levels of TNF-α, IL-6, MMP-2, MMP-9, desmosine, and cFN compared with mild-to-moderate OSA (all p < 0.05). SDC-1 reached statistical significance after BMI adjustment (p = 0.009). These biomarkers were positively associated with AHI, oxygen desaturation index (ODI), desaturation count, and time spent with SpO₂ <90% (T90), and inversely associated with N3 sleep duration. After adjustment for BMI, strong inter-biomarker partial correlations (r = 0.831-0.921, p < 0.001) formed a densely connected inflammatory-ECM cluster; this pattern remained significant, albeit more modest in magnitude, in sensitivity analyses using unadjusted Spearman correlations (ρ = 0.427-0.655, p < 0.001). GSH and MDA showed weaker and more isolated associations. OSA severity is associated with coordinated patterns among inflammatory and ECM-related biomarkers that parallel hypoxic burden and sleep architecture changes. In contrast, systemic oxidative stress markers appear less integrated within these patterns. These findings support the potential utility of multi-biomarker approaches in reflecting disease-related physiological alterations, potentially arising from both systemic and local upper airway tissue processes.

papers.title: Lived experiences and quality of life in people with severe, biologic-treated chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps: a hermeneutic phenomenological study.
papers.abstract: Chronic rhinosinusitis with nasal polyps (CRSwNP) is an inflammatory disease that affects quality of life. Diagnostic delays, symptom recurrence, and treatment failure increase the uncertainty and frustration of those affected. The objective of this study was to retrospectively explore the lived experiences of people with severe, biologic-treated CRSwNP from the onset of symptoms through to the failure of both appropriate medical therapy and surgery, in relation to the impact of the disease on their quality of life. A qualitative study based on Gadamer's hermeneutics was conducted. Between April 2024 and April 2025, 16 adults with severe biologic-treated CRSwNP participated in the study. They were selected through purposive sampling in a single airway clinic. Medical history was taken, nasal examination was performed, and imaging tests were undertaken, followed by in-depth interviews. Data were interpreted following a Gadamerian hermeneutic-circle approach, operationalised through Fleming's method. Three main themes were developed: (1) the silent burden of symptoms and their impact on daily life; (2) the odyssey to obtain a diagnosis; and (3) the experience of treatment failure and the associated emotional strain. People with severe, biologic-treated CRSwNP experience communication and sleep difficulties, impaired sex life, discrimination and self-medication, which substantially deteriorates their quality of life. This is compounded by diagnostic uncertainty, the need for self-management, treatment failure, and the ongoing search for information. Family support has a meaningful impact on their biopsychosocial well-being. These findings illustrate how physical, emotional and social dimensions are intertwined throughout this disease trajectory.

papers.title: Nasal symptoms are independently associated with subjective sleep impairment and symptom awareness in obstructive sleep apnea: an otolaryngology-based cohort study.
papers.abstract: Nasal disorders are common in obstructive sleep apnea (OSA). We previously reported an association between nasal symptoms and impaired sleep in non-obese OSA patients without multivariate adjustment. This study examined whether nasal symptoms are independently associated with subjective sleep quality and characterized the discordance phenotype in an otolaryngology-based cohort. This retrospective study included 628 OSA patients (AHI ≥ 5 events/h). Nasal symptoms were assessed using the JRQLQ. Sleep quality was measured by the ESS, AIS, and PSQI. Discordance was defined as AHI ≥ 30 events/h with absent subjective impairment (ESS ≤ 10, AIS ≤ 5, or PSQI ≤ 5). All questionnaire scores worsened with nasal symptom severity (all p < 0.001), whereas polysomnographic parameters did not differ. Nasal symptom score was independently associated with ESS ≥ 11 (OR 1.159), AIS ≥ 6 (OR 1.163), and PSQI ≥ 6 (OR 1.247; all p < 0.001); AHI was non-significant. Nasal obstruction retained significance for AIS ≥ 6 and PSQI ≥ 6 after adjustment. Objective nasal resistance did not correlate with symptoms (r = - 0.022). Discordance was present in 63.0% by ESS, rising to 90.3% at age ≥ 75 years. Nasal symptom score was associated with discordance across all definitions (OR 0.755-0.871; all p ≤ 0.027); AHI was non-significant. Nasal symptoms are independently associated with subjective sleep impairment in OSA beyond polysomnography-defined severity. Daytime rhinomanometry does not reflect nasal symptoms or sleep quality. Most patients with severe OSA lacked perceived impairment; nasal symptom burden was the only factor consistently associated with discordance. Multidimensional nasal and sleep assessment is recommended.

papers.title: Neurodevelopmental outcomes of infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia: a prospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: Therapeutic hypothermia (TH) is the standard of care for moderate to severe neonatal encephalopathy (NE). Although some centers consider TH for mild NE, neurodevelopmental outcomes of infants who do not meet eligibility criteria are incompletely defined. Infants evaluated for TH based on perinatal risk factors, but who did not meet institutional eligibility criteria, were prospectively enrolled. Neurodevelopmental outcomes were assessed at 24 months. Bayley-4 scores <85 were classified as sub-normative performance. Of 39 infants enrolled, 26 completed Bayley-4 assessments. Thirteen (50%) demonstrated sub-normative performance in at least one developmental domain; only one of them had an acute brain injury on MRI. Compared with infants with average-range performance, those with sub-normative performance had higher postnatal base deficits (10.1 vs 6 mmol/L, p 0.04), higher postnatal lactate levels (9.4 vs 4.9 mmol/L, p 0.05), and a trend toward less sleep-wake cycling on aEEG (45% vs 83%, p 0.06). A substantial proportion of infants evaluated for but not treated with TH demonstrated sub-normative developmental performance at 2 years. Absence of acute MRI-detected injury does not preclude later developmental vulnerability. These findings support longitudinal follow-up of infants who are evaluated for TH but do not meet TH criteria. Infants evaluated for but not treated with therapeutic hypothermia demonstrated a measurable risk of neurodevelopmental vulnerability at 2 years, with 50% demonstrating sub-normative performance (>1 SD below the normative mean) in at least one domain on the Bayley Scales of Infant and Toddler Development Fourth Edition. Early postnatal metabolic abnormalities in infants evaluated for therapeutic hypothermia showed a potential association with later developmental outcomes. There is a need for improved risk stratification and structured longitudinal follow-up for infants evaluated for but who do not meet cooling criteria.

papers.title: [Missed nursing care: a qualitative investigation of nurses' perceptions of patient outcomes].
papers.abstract: Missed nursing care (MNC) has emerged in recent years as an important area of research concerning the mechanisms that generate omissions or delays in the delivery of nursing care. MNC can negatively affect nursing-sensitive outcomes and is associated with a high incidence of adverse events, thereby affecting the quality and safety of patient care. To investigate the experiences of nurses working at ASST Valcamonica in relation to MNC, with particular attention to negative patient outcomes. A descriptive phenomenological qualitative study was conducted. Thirty-one narrative interviews were carried out with clinical nurses working in medical care settings at ASST Valcamonica. Participants were recruited through purposive sampling. The interviews were audio-recorded and analysed using Colaizzi's method. The analysis identified several themes: causes of missed nursing care, outcomes for nurses, outcomes for patients, and strategies for minimising missed nursing care. Pressure injuries, falls, infections and an increased occurrence of adverse events emerged as some of the most relevant patient outcomes. The findings are consistent with the existing literature, except for certain outcomes, including patients leaving the care setting without authorisation, alterations in the sleep-wake cycle, aspiration events and delirium, which require further investigation. The results also highlight the importance of promoting nursing leadership to improve the organisational climate and nurses' performance. Healthcare organisations should invest in human resources and educate nurses, beginning during their academic education, about missed nursing care and its negative consequences for patients.
